headline: Europe's first commercial orbital rocket launched by Isar Aerospace
summary: German company Isar Aerospace successfully sent its Spectrum rocket into low Earth orbit, marking a significant milestone for European spaceflight.
details: German company Isar Aerospace has achieved a major milestone by successfully launching Europe's first entirely commercial orbital rocket. The two-stage Spectrum rocket was sent into low Earth orbit from a Norwegian spaceport.

This successful launch follows a previous attempt in March that lasted only 30 seconds before the vehicle crashed and exploded. The company's perseverance has now paid off, securing a new option for commercial and institutional customers seeking space access.

Isar Aerospace CEO stated, "Today, Isar Aerospace opened space from Continental Europe. Launch continues to be the largest bottleneck for the global space industry and from today on, there is a true alternative for commercial and institutional customers… Europe now has sovereign access to space. We have entered into a new chapter for European spaceflight."

Previously, Europe relied heavily on Arianespace and Avio, which are largely government-funded. The current geopolitical climate, including the invasion of Ukraine cutting off Russian Soyuz rockets, makes sovereign European access to space increasingly important. The European Space Agency's policy to "buy European" further underscores the significance of this achievement.

Europe has its first commercial orbital rocket launch. Isar Aerospace's Spectrum rocket successfully reached low Earth orbit.

German company Isar Aerospace has achieved a major milestone by successfully launching Europe's first entirely commercial orbital rocket. The two-stage Spectrum rocket was sent into low Earth orbit from a Norwegian spaceport.

This successful launch follows a previous attempt in March that lasted only 30 seconds before the vehicle crashed and exploded. The company's perseverance has now paid off, securing a new option for commercial and institutional customers seeking space access.

Isar Aerospace CEO stated, "Today, Isar Aerospace opened space from Continental Europe. Launch continues to be the largest bottleneck for the global space industry and from today on, there is a true alternative for commercial and institutional customers… Europe now has sovereign access to space. We have entered into a new chapter for European spaceflight."

Previously, Europe relied heavily on Arianespace and Avio, which are largely government-funded. The current geopolitical climate, including the invasion of Ukraine cutting off Russian Soyuz rockets, makes sovereign European access to space increasingly important. The European Space Agency's policy to "buy European" further underscores the significance of this achievement.
